Subject: Re: cross-cloud burst routing feasibility and KV-cache considerations

Hey all — quick infrastructure readout:

- Cross-cloud burst routing (AWS/GCP) is viable as a short-term bridge; however, KV cache warm-start across cloud providers is non-trivial because we rely on local-GPU memory snapshots for fastest warm-up. Two options:
  1) Cold start optimization: optimize prompt templates and prewarm top 5% of prefixes to mitigate latency peak during migration (low operational overhead).
  2) Cache transfer: snapshot and transfer cache buckets via secured object storage before cutover — this requires ~24–36 hours prep and a brief routing freeze during final sync.

- Cost estimate: bridging on AWS spot-backed reserved capacity looks like +12–18% on unit cost for the first 4 weeks, plus a one-time engineering ops support window (~4 engineer-days).

Recommendation: pursue cold-start optimizations + a small prewarming window (option 1) to avoid the complexity of cross-cloud cache transfers unless Acme explicitly wants minimal latency delta.

Karthik
Head of Inference Infrastructure | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
